title: seed-library.sh: rebuild the curated library on a fresh machine from git
description:
Goal: one command that reproduces the curated library from a clone, as an alternative to cloning production. The user hand-curates, so the catalog (crates/apricity-sources/catalog/sources.json + samples/sources.json) is the record of what was approved; the seed must rebuild everything else from it.

Steps to chain: (1) apricity sources fetch --all (sha256-verified); (2) denoise + analyze the LoC/CC folders with apricity_analyze --denoise (neural:medium default); (3) apricity migrate --from . --to <library> (deterministic, idempotent); (4) optionally apricity sync push --library <dir> --bucket <b>, then the admin runs Import library from bucket.

Gaps to close first/along the way: 
- apricitus-b16b5d: migration does not map loc/... or .clean.wav paths (new imports would land in uploads).
- Pin the denoiser model version/checksum (dns64 weights are fetched unpinned) and record it, so clean copies are reproducible; record the recipe (already in manifest source.denoise).
- ccMixter/Internet Archive importer does not exist yet; ccMixter audio needs a Referer of ccmixter.org (403 otherwise).
- .clean.wav files are gitignored derived audio: the seed regenerates them.
Verify by seeding into a scratch dir and diffing against the working library (scripts/check-migration.sh already renders example scores from a migrated library). Spec first, scripts + docs/tools.md entry.
